nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)₂ synthesis
nodes.procedure: A commercial NF piece (3 cm × 1 cm) was cleaned using ethanol and deionized (DI) water through ultrasonication, with each step for 15 minutes. Ni(NO₃)₂·6H₂O of 1.0 mM, 5 mM of urea, and 2 mM of NH₄F were dissolved in 20 mL of deionized water. Afterward, a precleaned NF piece (3 cm × 1 cm) was placed at the bottom of an autoclave and immersed in the prepared solution. The autoclave was then sealed and heated to 90°C for 10 h. After cooling to room temperature, the nickel hydroxide-coated NF piece was thoroughly rinsed with deionized water three times and dried overnight at 80°C in an electric oven.

nodes.name: PBA nanocube formation
nodes.procedure: The chemical K₃[Fe(CN)₆] (X = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 1.0 mM) was dissolved in 30 mL of deionized water. Subsequently, the prepared solution was transferred to an autoclave containing an NF piece that was coated with nickel hydroxide. The autoclave was tightly sealed and subjected to heat at 90°C for 24 h. Following this, the Ni(OH)₂PBA on the NF was removed and rinsed using deionized water and ethanol. This process was repeated three times before the Ni(OH)₂PBA nanosheets on the NF was dried in an electric oven at 80°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Phosphidation of precursors
nodes.procedure: The Ni(OH)₂PBA nanosheets on NF was subjected to direct phosphidation at 350°C for 2 h using 0.5 g of NaH₂PO₂·H₂O under a nitrogen flow. After cooling to room temperature, Fe-doped Ni₂P nanosheets were obtained on NF. Additionally, by varying the precursors of K₃[Fe(CN)₆] (X = 0.25, 0.50, 0.75 and 1.0 mM), the Fe-doped Ni₂P nanosheets catalysts were synthesized following the same procedures as mentioned above. The NF surface was transformed into Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets using hydrothermal treatment at 90°C for 10 h. Then, Prussian blue analogues (PBA) nanocubes were simply synthesized and attached to the Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets through a kinetically regulated crystallization process at 90°C for 24 h.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH seawater
nodes.source_text: In a 1.0 M KOH seawater electrolyte, Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) nanosheets, when used as an electrocatalyst for the OER and HER, require overpotentials of 310 (390) and 262 (342) mV to achieve current densities of 100 and 500 mA cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.description: HER comparison of different Fe doping concentrations in 1.0 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Out of different Fe doping concentrations like Fe-doped Ni₂P nanosheets with 0.75 mM, 0.50 mM, and 0.25 mM, the Fe-doped Ni₂P nanosheets with a concentration of 1.0 mM exhibited the highest HER activity (Figure S22, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) nanosheets show rough plates with numerous Fe nanocubes ~50 nm distributed on 5 μm diameter sheets, maintaining 3D porous framework of Ni foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the concentration of PBA was increased from 0 to 1.0 mM, the previously smooth Ni₂P structure transformed completely into rough plates with numerous nanocubes, as can be seen in Figure 2B-F.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) nanosheets maintain original morphologies with increased surface roughness due to Fe particles within 50 nm dimension; polycrystalline structure confirmed by SAED.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) analysis, shown in Figure 3A,B, demonstrates that the Fe-doped Ni₂P nanosheets maintained their original morphologies after phosphorization.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows crystalline nanosheet matrix with amorphous Fe nanoparticles; interplanar spacing of 0.227 nm corresponds to (111) plane of Ni₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The precise measurement of the interplanar spacings within the lattice fringes located at the core of every crystalline nanoparticle revealed a value of 0.227, related to the (111) plane of Ni₂P as depicted in Figure 3E.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX confirms homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, P, N, C, O elements across Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The spectrum obtained from EDX, and color mapping shown in Figure 2G-O, reveals the presence of Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) nanosheets with a homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, P, N, C, and O elements across the nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD of Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) shows Ni₂P phase peaks at 40.8°, 47.2°, 54.2°, 55.0° (111), (210), (300), (211) planes with (111) peak shifted 0.15° to smaller angle vs pure Ni₂P; no Fe₂P peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of Fe_x-doped Ni₂P (x = 1.0 mM) nanosheets exhibited a series of distinct diffraction peaks at 40.8, 47.2, 54.2, and 55.0°, which matched the (111), (210), (300), and (211) Ni₂P phase structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows D (1357 cm⁻¹) and G (1590 cm⁻¹) bands indicating amorphous carbon/graphene-like structures in Fe-doped Ni₂P@NF derived from PBA phosphidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectroscopy results of the Fe-doped Ni₂P@NF show distinct peaks at 1357 and 1590 cm⁻¹, representing the characteristic D and G bands of the amorphous structure and carbon materials with graphitic sp² hybridization, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows peaks at 853.0/870.7 eV (Niδ+), 856.3/874.0 eV (Ni²+) with 0.2 eV blue shift vs Ni₂P indicating electron transfer from Fe to Ni; P 2p at 129.5/131.0 eV; Fe 2p at 711.4/723.5 eV confirms doped structure without Fe-P phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distinct peak observed at 853.0/870.7 eV in the detailed XPS analysis of the Ni 2p orbital (Figure 4C) is identified as Ni ions with a charge of Niδ+ ... comparing the Ni 2p3/2 peaks of Fe-doped Ni₂P and non-doped Ni₂P samples demonstrates a BE blue shift of about 0.2 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) is 89.59 m²/g with mesoporous structure (type IV hysteresis, ~6.5 nm pore diameter).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) technique was employed to determine the surface area of Fe-doped Ni₂P, resulting in a value of 89.59 m²g⁻¹ (Figure 4F).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at 300 mV overpotential (OER) shows R_ct ≈ 1.1 Ω for Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) vs 1.28 Ω Ni₂P; at 250 mV (HER) R_ct = 4.98 Ω vs 13.28 Ω Ni₂P.
nodes.evidence_snippet: All of these electrocatalysts displayed low charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) when supported by conductive nickel foam. Specifically, the Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) nanosheets material displayed R_ct of ≈ 1.1Ω, lower than Ni₂P nanosheets (1.28Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS-derived double-layer capacitance C_dl = 32.07 mF cm⁻² for OER and 4.52 mF cm⁻² for HER of Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM), highest among tested catalysts indicating largest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Among the different samples analyzed (Figure 5E), the heterogeneous Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) nanosheets demonstrate the highest double-layer capacitance (C_dl) at 32.07 mF cm⁻² ... In Figure 6D, it is evident that our Fe-doped Ni₂P (1.0 mM) nanosheets catalyst shows the highest C_dl value of 4.52 mF cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during seawater OER shows NiOOH peaks at 464 cm⁻¹ and 523 cm⁻¹ increasing with applied voltage (1.54-1.61 V vs RHE).
nodes.evidence_snippet: An in situ Raman analysis was performed at various potentials ... Elevating the voltage from 1.54 to 1.61 V versus RHE resulted in unique peaks at 464 cm⁻¹ and 523 cm⁻¹, indicating Ni-O vibrations of NiOOH.
